source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. XII (Montreuil)

20.title: PROSECUTIO EXPOSITIONIS PRÆSENTIS VICESIMI CAPITULI : QUUM SERO ESSET DIE ILLA, UNA SABBATORUM.
20.title_en: Continuation of the exposition of this twentieth chapter: When it was late that same day, the first of the week

paras.t: HOC loco describit Evangelista quintam Christi apparitionem, factam in die Paschæ, et etiam sextam, quæ facta est præsente Thoma, in octava Paschæ. Quinquies enim apparuit Christus in die Paschæ : Primo, Magdalenæ, quemadmodum in Marco legitur : Surgens Jesus mane prima sabbati, apparuit primo Mariæ Magdalene. Secundo, mulieribus redeuntibus a sepulcro, juxta illud Matthæi : Ecce Jesus occurrit illis, dicens, Avete. Tertio, Petro, quamvis locus ignoretur; creditur tamen quod redeunti a monumento. Quarto, duobus discipulis euntibus in Emmaus, secundum quod recitat Lucas. Quinto, undecim Apostolis in conclavi, sicut nunc contestatur Joannes.
paras.en: In this place the Evangelist describes the fifth appearance of Christ, made on the day of the Pasch, and also the sixth, which was made with Thomas present, on the octave of the Pasch. For Christ appeared five times on the day of the Pasch. First, to Magdalen, as is read in Mark: [[Mark 16:9|But he rising early the first day of the week, appeared first to Mary Magdalen|Surgens Jesus mane prima sabbati, apparuit primo Mariæ Magdalene]]. Second, to the women returning from the sepulchre, according to that of Matthew: [[Matt 28:9|behold, Jesus met them, saying: All hail|Ecce Jesus occurrit illis, dicens, Avete]]. Third, to Peter[[Luke 24:34||]][[1 Cor 15:5||]], though the place is unknown; yet it is believed that it was as he returned from the tomb. Fourth, to the two disciples going to Emmaus, as Luke recounts[[Luke 24:13||]]. Fifth, to the eleven Apostles in the closed room, as John now bears witness.

paras.t: Quum sero esset, hoc est hora vespertina, et nocte incipiente, die illa, in qua apparuit Magdalenæ, una sabbatorum, id est, quæ dies fuit una dierum illius hebdomadæ, qui omnes dicebantur sabbata, quia festivi, et fores, id est januæ, essent clausæ, ubi erant discipuli, hoc est Apostoli, et etiam alii, secundum Lucam, congregati propter metum Judæorum : in quo patet eorum infirmitas, qui timebant eos qui corpus potuerunt occidere. Dicunt quidam, quod Apostoli erant dispersi in die propter metum Judæorum, sed de sero conveniebant ad locum unum. Evangelista vero nunc dicit, quod erant congregati propter metum prædictum. Lucas quoque habet, quod mulieres regressæ a monumento, nuntiaverunt quæ audierunt illis undecim : quod fuit clara die, quia post hoc Petrus et Joannes cucurrerunt ad monumentum. Ex quibus patet, quod discipuli etiam in die sederunt collecti januis clausis, propter metum Judæorum : imo minus audebant exire diebus quam noctibus.
paras.en: [[20:19|Now when it was late|Cum ergo sero esset]], that is, at the evening hour, as night was beginning, [[20:19|the same day|die illo]], on which He appeared to Magdalen, [[20:19|the first of the week|una sabbatorum]], that is, the day which was one of the days of that week, all of which were called sabbaths because they were festal, [[20:19|and the doors were shut, where the disciples were|et fores essent clausæ, ubi erant discipuli]], that is, the Apostles, and others too, according to Luke[[Luke 24:33||]], [[20:19|gathered together, for fear of the Jews|congregati propter metum Judæorum]]: in which their weakness is plain, who feared those who could kill the body[[Matt 10:28||]]. Some say that the Apostles were scattered by day for fear of the Jews, but in the evening came together to one place. But the Evangelist now says that they were gathered together for the said fear. Luke also has it that the women, returning from the tomb, told what they had heard to the eleven[[Luke 24:9||]]: which was in broad day, since after this Peter and John ran to the tomb[[Luke 24:12||]]. From which it is plain that the disciples sat gathered with the doors shut even by day, for fear of the Jews: indeed they dared go out less by day than by night.

paras.t: Venit Jesus ostio clauso, per penetrationem dimensionum. Corpora enim glorificata omnia penetrant per dotem subtilitatis, secundum quosdam : non tamen sine grandi miraculo, prout Thomas super quartum Sententiarum satis demonstrat. Quemadmodum igitur Jesus exivit uterum Matris, ea integra remanente, sic intravit et exiit domum non apertam, divina omnipotente virtute. Et stetit in medio discipulorum. Ipse namque est mediator, doctor reconciliatorque noster, ideo competebat ei esse in medio, sicut et ante passionem locutus est : Ego in medio vestrum sum. Magister quippe virtutum, medium semper elegit, quia in medio virtus consistit. Quomodo autem factum sit quod nunc refert Joannes, Lucas plenius edocet : quo legitur, quod quum Jesus cognitus fuisset a duobus discipulis in fractione panis, et disparuisset, illi surgentes regressi sunt in Jerusalem eadem hora, inveneruntque undecim congregatos, et eos qui cum illis erant, quibus dixerunt quomodo Jesus apparuisset eis in via, et qualiter eum cognoverunt : quibus ista narrantibus, venit Jesus, et stetit in medio discipulorum.
paras.en: [[20:19|Jesus came|venit Jesus]] with the door shut, by penetration of dimensions [[that is, two bodies occupying the same place]]. For glorified bodies penetrate all things by the endowment of subtlety, according to some: yet not without a great miracle, as Thomas amply shows on the fourth book of the Sentences. As therefore Jesus came forth from His Mother's womb while she remained intact, so He entered and left the unopened house by the almighty power of God. [[20:19|And stood in the midst|et stetit in medio]] of the disciples. For He is our mediator, teacher and reconciler, and so it befitted Him to be in the midst, as He also said before the passion: [[Luke 22:27|I am in the midst of you|Ego in medio vestrum sum]]. For the Master of the virtues always chose the mean, since virtue consists in the mean. How what John now relates came about, Luke teaches more fully: where it is read that when Jesus had been known by the two disciples in the breaking of bread and had vanished[[Luke 24:30||]], they rose up and returned to Jerusalem the same hour, and found the eleven gathered together, [[Luke 24:33|and those that were with them|et eos qui cum illis erant]], to whom they told how Jesus had appeared to them on the way and how they knew Him[[Luke 24:35||]]: and as they were telling these things, Jesus came and stood in the midst of the disciples[[Luke 24:36||]].

paras.t: Et dixit eis : Pax vobis. Quod docuit Christus, hoc fecit. Præcepit autem discipulis : In quamcumque domum intraveritis, primum dicite : Pax huic domui. Hinc ipse domum ingrediens in qua erant carissimi sui electissimique discipuli, ait : Pax vobis. Rursus, sic eos salutavit, quoniam paulo ante, in qua nocte tradebatur, disseruit : Pacem relinquo vobis. Quod igitur tunc reliquit, nunc attulit, dedit et auxit. Discipuli quoque pace maxime indigebant, quoniam multipliciter conturbati erant, ac territi, videlicet propter præteritam Christi passionem, propter Judæorum crudelitatem, et proprii cordis quamdam hæsitationem de Christi resurrectione, de cujus veritate nondum fuerant roborati. Insuper sic salutavit discipulos, quoniam pax est maximum bonum, omnique Christiano præcipue appetendum : per quam homines fiunt filii Dei, quemadmodum scriptum est : Beati pacifici, quoniam filii Dei vocabuntur. Propter quod ait Dionysius, quod omnia appetunt pacem, et propter hanc agunt omne quod agunt. Ex quo concluditur, quod pax est vel ipsa beatitudo, vel proxima ad beatitudinem dispositio.
paras.en: [[20:19|and said to them: Peace be to you|et dixit eis: Pax vobis]]. What Christ taught, that He did. For He commanded the disciples: [[Luke 10:5|Into whatever house you enter, first say: Peace be to this house|In quamcumque domum intraveritis, primum dicite : Pax huic domui]]. Hence He Himself, entering the house in which were His dearest and most chosen disciples, says: Peace be to you. Again, He so greeted them because a little before, on the night He was betrayed, He had said: [[John 14:27|Peace I leave with you|Pacem relinquo vobis]]. What He left then, therefore, He now brought, gave and increased. The disciples too were in the greatest need of peace, since they were troubled and frightened in many ways: by the passion of Christ now past, by the cruelty of the Jews, and by a certain hesitation of their own hearts about Christ's resurrection, of whose truth they had not yet been made firm. Moreover, He so greeted the disciples because peace is the greatest good, to be sought above all by every Christian: through which men become sons of God, as it is written: [[Matt 5:9|Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.|Beati pacifici: quoniam filii Dei vocabuntur.]]. Wherefore Dionysius says that all things seek peace, and for its sake do all that they do. From which it is concluded that peace is either beatitude itself, or the disposition nearest to beatitude.

paras.t: Christus autem præsertim nunc loquitur de pace interna, quæ est tranquillitas animi, utpote quies a motibus propriis inordinatis, videlicet a timore immoderato, a tristitia sæculi, quæ secundum Apostolum, mortem operatur, a dolore rationem impediente. Non enim optavit discipulis quietem ab exterioribus persecutionibus ad tempus, quos in medio luporum erat missurus, sed ut in omni turbatione extrinseca conservarent pacem internam. Propterea ad Hebræos monet Apostolus : Pacem sequimini et sanctimoniam, sine qua nemo Deum videbit.
paras.en: But Christ is here speaking chiefly of inward peace, which is tranquillity of mind, namely rest from one's own disordered motions: from immoderate fear, from the sorrow of the world, which, according to the Apostle, worketh death[[2 Cor 7:10||]], from grief that hinders reason. For He did not wish His disciples rest from outward persecutions for the time, since He was about to send them into the midst of wolves[[Matt 10:16||]], but that amid every outward disturbance they might keep inward peace. Hence the Apostle admonishes the Hebrews: [[Heb 12:14|Follow peace with all men and holiness: without which no man shall see God|Pacem sequimini et sanctimoniam, sine qua nemo Deum videbit]].

paras.t: Et quum hoc dixisset, ostendit eis manus et latus, forte et pedes : imo et pedes, ut infra ex verbis Lucæ evangelistæ patebit. In his quinque vulnerum remanserunt cicatrices, in testimonium identitatis corporis passi, resuscitati, et glorificati, itemque in signum victoriæ Salvatoris. Ostendit ergo discipulis manus perfossas, et latus lancea perforatum, ut scirent quod ipse esset qui paulo ante pendebat in ligno, et quod idem numero corpus resumpsisset. — Multa hoc loco omittit Joannes, quæ recitat Lucas; ea quoque quæ Lucas omisit, supplevit Joannes. Itaque Luca testante, Christus discipulis dixit : Videte manus meas et pedes meos; palpate et videte, quoniam spiritus carnem et ossa non habet, sicut me videtis habere. Et alia multa in hac apparitione dicta et facta recitat Lucas.
paras.en: [[20:20|And when he had said this, he shewed them his hands and his side|Et cum hoc dixisset, ostendit eis manus et latus]], perhaps the feet too: indeed the feet too, as will appear below from the words of Luke the Evangelist. In these the scars of the five wounds remained, in witness of the identity of the body that suffered, was raised and was glorified, and also as a sign of the Saviour's victory. He showed the disciples, then, the pierced hands and the side opened by the lance, that they might know that He was the one who a little before hung on the wood, and that He had taken again the body numerically the same. — Many things John omits in this place which Luke recounts; and what Luke omitted, John supplied. So, by Luke's witness, Christ said to the disciples: [[Luke 24:39|See my hands and feet, that it is I myself. Handle, and see: for a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as you see me to have|Videte manus meas et pedes meos; palpate et videte, quoniam spiritus carnem et ossa non habet, sicut me videtis habere]]. And Luke recounts many other things said and done in this appearance[[Luke 24:36||]].

paras.t: Gavisi sunt ergo discipuli, viso Domino dominorum, qui in femore suo scriptum habet : Rex regum et Dominus dominantium. Gaudium nempe est diffusio animi in conceptione boni, oriturque ex unione potentiæ cum bono convenienti. Quoniam ergo discipuli viderunt Jesum, summum et convenientissimum bonum, quem maxime diligebant, de cujus passione vehementer dolebant, cujus beatitudini cordialiter congratulabantur : ideo viso eo, ultra quam æstimari posset aut exprimi, lætabantur. Gavisi sunt autem propter Jesum, et propter se ipsos : quia magistro suo intime congaudebant ; et de suo profectu exhilarati sunt, videntes se non esse deceptos sequendo Jesum, propter quem omnia sua reliquerunt, et multa perpessi fuerunt ac patiebantur.
paras.en: [[20:20|The disciples therefore were glad, when they saw the Lord|Gavisi sunt ergo discipuli, viso Domino]] of lords, who hath on His thigh written: [[Apoc 19:16|KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS|Rex regum et Dominus dominantium]]. For joy is the expansion of the mind in the conceiving of a good, and arises from the union of a power with a fitting good. Since, then, the disciples saw Jesus, the highest and most fitting good, whom they loved most, for whose passion they grieved vehemently, in whose beatitude they heartily rejoiced with Him: therefore, seeing Him, they were glad beyond what could be reckoned or expressed. They rejoiced for Jesus' sake and for their own: because they rejoiced inwardly with their Master; and they were cheered at their own advancement, seeing that they had not been deceived in following Jesus, for whom they had left all they had[[Matt 19:27||]], and had suffered and were suffering much.

paras.t: Dixit ergo eis iterum : Pax vobis. Siquidem viso Domino Jesu, conturbati fuerunt atque conterriti, juxta Lucam : ideo repetit, Pax vobis. Quæ etiam repetitio, confirmationis indicium est, dilectionisque signum, et admonitio discipulorum ut pacem jugiter appetant, præcipueque exquirant. Vel, ideo bis ait, Pax vobis, quia optavit eis pacem gratiæ in præsenti, et pacem gloriæ in futuro. Sicut misit me Pater, et ego mitto vos : id est, quemadmodum Pater misit me ex vera caritate et pietate, ad prædicandum Evangelium vitæ Judæis, a quibus multas persecutiones, et tandem amarissimam perpessus sum mortem, quorum tamen hominum nonnullos converti; sic ego nunc mittam vos ad prædicandum evangelicam legem Judæis ac gentibus, ex caritate et pietate ad vos, et item ad illos, a quibus multa adversa et mortem sustinebitis, quosdam vero eorum convertetis.
paras.en: [[20:21|He said therefore to them again: Peace be to you|Dixit ergo eis iterum: Pax vobis]]. For on seeing the Lord Jesus they were troubled and terrified, according to Luke[[Luke 24:37||]]: therefore He repeats, Peace be to you. This repetition too is a token of confirmation and a sign of love, and an admonition to the disciples to seek peace constantly and to pursue it above all. Or, He says Peace be to you twice because He wished them the peace of grace in the present and the peace of glory in the future. [[20:21|As the Father hath sent me, I also send you|Sicut misit me Pater, et ego mitto vos]]: that is, as the Father sent Me out of true charity and loving-kindness to preach the Gospel of life to the Jews, from whom I suffered many persecutions and at last a most bitter death, and yet some of whom I converted; so I now will send you to preach the law of the Gospel to Jews and Gentiles, out of charity and loving-kindness towards you and likewise towards them, from whom you will endure many adversities and death, but some of whom you will convert.

paras.t: Hæc quum dixisset, insufflavit, et dixit eis : Accipite Spiritum Sanctum. Postquam Salvator dixit discipulis, Sicut misit me Pater, et ego mitto vos, infudit discipulis Spiritum Sanctum, quia officium prædicationis quod eis commisit, sine speciali gratia Spiritus Sancti expleri non valuit. Oportet enim ut prædicator verbi cœlestis, in se ipso abundet caritatis fervore, et sapientia divinorum, quatenus ignita proferat verba, motiva et penetrativa, sitque sententiosus, discretus et instructivus in sermonibus suis. Denique, per corporalem illam insufflationem et inspirationem, evidenter signavit superintellectualem atque æternam processionem seu spirationem qua Spiritus Sanctus ab ipso procedit, prout plenius probat Anselmus in libro de Processione Spiritus Sancti. Rursus, dicendo, Accipite Spiritum Sanctum, insinuavit se per auctoritatem dare Spiritum Sanctum : quod nequaquam sic esset, nisi Spiritus Sanctus ab ipso procederet. Sed nonne Apostoli ante hanc horam habuerunt Spiritum Sanctum? Habuerunt utique, non autem tam copiose et efficaciter, seu ad tot tantosque effectus, ut ex hac hora, quia et nunc data est omnibus eis potestas ligandi atque solvendi, sicut mox introducetur.
paras.en: [[20:22|When he had said this, he breathed on them; and he said to them: Receive ye the Holy Ghost|Hæc cum dixisset, insufflavit, et dixit eis: Accipite Spiritum Sanctum]]. After the Saviour had said to the disciples, As the Father hath sent me, I also send you, He poured the Holy Ghost into them, because the office of preaching which He committed to them could not be fulfilled without a special grace of the Holy Ghost. For the preacher of the heavenly word must abound in himself with the fervour of charity and with wisdom in divine things, so that he may utter fiery words, moving and piercing, and be weighty, discerning and instructive in his sermons. Further, by that bodily breathing and inbreathing He plainly signified the supra-intellectual and eternal procession or spiration by which the Holy Ghost proceeds from Him, as Anselm proves more fully in his book On the Procession of the Holy Ghost. Again, by saying, Receive ye the Holy Ghost, He intimated that He gives the Holy Ghost by authority: which would by no means be so unless the Holy Ghost proceeded from Him. But did not the Apostles have the Holy Ghost before this hour? They did indeed, but not so abundantly and effectively, or for so many and such great effects, as from this hour, since now too the power of binding and loosing was given to them all, as will shortly be brought in.

paras.t: Augustinus facit hic grandem quæstionem, cujus se solutionem nescire fatetur. Quærit ergo, cur Christus bis dedit Spiritum Sanctum, semel in terra ante ascensionem, et semel de cœlo post ascensionem. Tangit autem Augustinus quamdam solutionem sub dubio, puta quod ideo, quoniam duo sunt præcepta caritatis. Quam rationem Gregorius et Beda affirmant esse hujus rei causam, videlicet, quod in terra dedit, ut diligatur proximus, deinde de cœlo, ut diligatur Deus. Sed quia per eamdem gratiam utrumque præceptum impletur, nec unum sine alio valet impleri, imo et unus est habitus caritatis qua Deus proximusque diligitur, ideo potest alia ratio assignari. Ut enim Dionysius docet, Natura non procedit a distanti in distans, nisi per medium. Quem processum auctor naturæ Deus sublimis et benedictus, observat frequenter, præsertim quum teste Apostolo, Quæ a Deo sunt, ordinata sunt. Unde et admonet : Omnia decenter et secundum ordinem fiant in vobis. Hinc ergo Christus sapientia Patris, disponens universa suaviter, suos discipulos paulatim ad sublimiora attollens, ac pedetentim ad perfectionem perducens, primo dedit eis Spiritum Sanctum in terra per insufflationem, non in tanta plenitudine, nec in signo tam evidenti ut postea, quatenus per istam ad illam exuberantissimam Spiritus Sancti susceptionem quæ facta est in die sancto Pentecostes, disponerentur.
paras.en: Augustine here raises a great question, the solution of which he confesses he does not know. He asks, then, why Christ gave the Holy Ghost twice, once on earth before the ascension and once from heaven after the ascension. Augustine touches, though doubtfully, on one solution: namely that it was because there are two precepts of charity. This reason Gregory and Bede affirm to be the cause of the matter: that He gave the Spirit on earth that our neighbour may be loved, and then from heaven that God may be loved. But since both precepts are fulfilled by the same grace, and one cannot be fulfilled without the other, and indeed there is one habit of charity by which God and neighbour are loved, another reason can be assigned. For as Dionysius teaches, nature does not proceed from one extreme to another except through a mean. This procedure God, the sublime and blessed author of nature, frequently observes, especially since, as the Apostle witnesses, [[Rom 13:1|those that are ordained of God|Quæ a Deo sunt, ordinata sunt]]. Whence he also admonishes: [[1 Cor 14:40|let all things be done decently and according to order|Omnia decenter et secundum ordinem]] among you. Hence Christ, the wisdom of the Father[[1 Cor 1:24||]], ordering all things sweetly[[Wis 8:1||]], raising His disciples little by little to higher things and leading them step by step to perfection, first gave them the Holy Ghost on earth by breathing, not in such fullness nor with so evident a sign as afterwards, so that by this they might be disposed for that most overflowing reception of the Holy Ghost which took place on the holy day of Pentecost.

paras.t: Quorum remiseritis peccata, eos legitime absolvendo, et divinæ virtuti, quæ sola dimittit peccata ut causa principalis, instrumentaliter vi clavium cooperando, remittuntur eis a Deo, saltem quoad culpam, non tamen semper aut totaliter quantum ad pœnam. Tamen, per orationem sacerdotis virtutemque clavium, et per pudorem ac contritionem confitentis, aliquid pœnæ dimittitur, tanto utique amplius, quanto pudor et contritio fuerint fortiores. Possent enim esse tam magni, quod tota pœna dimitteretur. Et quorum peccata retinueritis, id est, non dimiseritis, sed retinenda judicaveritis, eo quod non vere pœniteant, nec dignos se præbeant ad indulgentiam obtinendam, retenta sunt, id est, Deus illa imputabit hominibus talibus. Oportet itaque ut judicium Ecclesiæ conformetur divino judicio, servando videlicet rectum processum, et debitum clavium usum. Unde ultimo Ecclesiasticæ hierarchiæ capitulo, ait Theologus : Sacerdotes hierarchicis sibi collatis virtutibus uti oportet, prout Deitas moverit eos. Agens enim instrumentale non sortitur efficaciam, nisi secundum quod a principali causa movetur. Propter quod profitetur Apostolus : Secundum potestatem quæ data est mihi in ædificationem, et non in destructionem.
paras.en: [[20:23|Whose sins you shall forgive|Quorum remiseritis peccata]], by lawfully absolving them, and cooperating instrumentally by the power of the keys with the divine power, which alone forgives sins as principal cause, [[20:23|they are forgiven them|remittuntur eis]] by God, at least as to the guilt, though not always or wholly as to the punishment. Yet by the prayer of the priest and the power of the keys, and by the shame and contrition of the penitent, something of the punishment is remitted, and the more so the stronger the shame and contrition are. For they could be so great that the whole punishment would be remitted. [[20:23|And whose sins you shall retain|Et quorum retinueritis]], that is, do not forgive, but judge must be retained, because they do not truly repent nor show themselves worthy to obtain pardon, [[20:23|they are retained|retenta sunt]], that is, God will impute them to such men. The judgement of the Church, therefore, must be conformed to the divine judgement, by keeping a right procedure and the due use of the keys. Whence in the last chapter of the Ecclesiastical Hierarchy the Theologian [[that is, Dionysius]] says: Priests must use the hierarchical powers conferred on them as the Godhead moves them. For an instrumental agent has no efficacy except as it is moved by the principal cause. Wherefore the Apostle professes: [[2 Cor 13:10|according to the power which the Lord hath given me unto edification and not unto destruction|Secundum potestatem quæ data est mihi in ædificationem, et non in destructionem]].

paras.t: Itaque Christus nunc ait et confert universis Apostolis, quod ante passionem Petro singulariter dixit : Quodcumque, inquiens, ligaveris super terram, erit ligatum et in cœlis ; et quodcumque solveris super terram, erit solutum et in cœlis. Ideo autem Petro tanquam principaliori inter Apostolos et capiti universalis Ecclesiæ, hoc dictum est singulariter, ut quum sit ordo in Ecclesia, hæc potestas credatur primo ac principaliter residere in summo Pontifice, S. Petri vicario, atque ab ipso derivari in archiepiscopos et episcopos, et ab ipsis tanquam a mediis, in simplices sacerdotes. Verumtamen, quamvis omnis sacerdos in sua ordinatione ligandi ac solvendi potestatem recipiat, quum secundum Thomam, realiter idem sint character sacerdotalis, et potestas prædicta, quæ etiam clavis vocatur; non tamen habet hujus potestatis exsecutionem, nisi ei subjiciatur materia, scilicet homines super quos sibi jurisdictio detur, seu cura animarum committatur a superiore, qui sicut dat eam inferiori, sic potest eam ei auferre in toto vel parte, legitima causa occurrente.
paras.en: So Christ now says to, and confers on, all the Apostles what before the passion He said to Peter singly: [[Matt 16:19|whatsoever thou shalt bind upon earth, it shall be bound also in heaven|Quodcumque … ligaveris … et in cœlis]]. It was said to Peter singly, as the chief among the Apostles and head of the universal Church, so that, there being order in the Church, this power may be believed to reside first and principally in the supreme Pontiff, the vicar of St Peter, and to be derived from him to archbishops and bishops, and from them, as intermediaries, to simple priests. Nevertheless, although every priest receives in his ordination the power of binding and loosing, since according to Thomas the priestly character and the said power, which is also called the key, are really the same, yet he does not have the exercise of this power unless matter is subjected to him, namely men over whom jurisdiction is given him, or the care of souls is committed to him by a superior; who, as he gives it to the inferior, so can take it from him in whole or in part, when a lawful cause arises.

paras.t: Præterea, Christus dicendo discipulis, Quorum remiseritis peccata, etc., manifeste ostendit se esse verum Deum, qui solus potest tantam conferre potestatem hominibus, quæ nec angelis data est. Decuit autem ut postquam Deus assumpsit humanam naturam, homines ab illo acciperent divinam virtutem, et supernaturalem quamdam deificationem : quod maxime datum est sacerdotibus, per hoc quod sunt dispensatores sacramentorum novæ legis, in quibus gratia continetur et datur. Omnibus quoque fidelibus datur deificatio talis, per diversa dona et gratiam Spiritus Sancti, secundum quod in epistola canonica Petri inducitur : Maxima et pretiosa nobis promissa donavit, ut per hæc efficiamini divinæ consortes naturæ. — Postremo, de hac materia, et quid sit clavis, et quomodo sacerdos evangelicæ legis dicatur peccata dimittere, an scilicet aliquid cooperando, vel dumtaxat ostendendo, de verbis quoque Hieronymi circa hoc, plurima dixi super Matthæum : quæ non sunt hoc loco repetenda, quamvis ista sine illis plene intelligi nequeant.
paras.en: Further, Christ, by saying to the disciples, Whose sins you shall forgive, etc., plainly showed Himself to be true God, who alone can confer on men so great a power, one not given even to the angels. And it was fitting that, after God had assumed human nature, men should receive from Him a divine power and a certain supernatural deification: which is given above all to priests, in that they are dispensers of the sacraments of the new law, in which grace is contained and given. Such deification is also given to all the faithful, through the divers gifts and grace of the Holy Ghost, as is set down in the canonical epistle of Peter: [[2 Pet 1:4|he hath given us most great and precious promises: that by these you may be made partakers of the divine nature|Maxima et pretiosa nobis promissa donavit, ut per hæc efficiamini divinæ consortes naturæ]]. — Lastly, on this matter, what the key is, how the priest of the Gospel law is said to forgive sins, whether by cooperating in some way or only by declaring, and on Jerome's words about it, I said a great deal on Matthew[[Matt 16:19||]]: which is not to be repeated here, though these things cannot be fully understood without it.

paras.t: Dedit itaque Christus Apostolis eorumque successoribus divinam et admirabilem potestatem, qua alios possunt solvere et ligare, a regno excludere, et in illud inducere. Sed videant ministri Ecclesiæ ut tanta virtute digne utantur, exsistendo in gratia, causasque confitentium sapienter pensando ac discernendo, et privatum amorem ac odium, ceterasque inordinatas affectiones penitus repellendo : quoniam si indignos absolvant, vel dignos ligent, dicetur de eis illud Ezechielis : Interfecerunt animas quæ non moriuntur, et vivificabant animas quæ non vivunt.
paras.en: So Christ gave the Apostles and their successors a divine and wonderful power, by which they can loose and bind others, shut them out of the kingdom and bring them into it. But let the ministers of the Church see that they use so great a power worthily, being in grace, weighing and discerning wisely the cases of those who confess, and wholly casting out private love and hatred and other disordered affections: for if they absolve the unworthy or bind the worthy, that word of Ezechiel will be said of them: [[Ezech 13:19|to kill souls which should not die, and to save souls alive which should not live|Interfecerunt animas quæ non moriuntur, et vivificabant animas quæ non vivunt]] [[that is, They killed souls which do not die, and quickened souls which do not live]].

paras.t: Thomas autem unus ex duodecim, hoc est unus Apostolorum, qui ante passionem Christi erant duodecim, quando Judas fuit unus illorum ; vel, Unus ex duodecim, quia dum Joannes evangelium præsens descripsit, successit Mathias in locum Judæ, sicque Thomas fuit unus Apostolorum, qui Mathia electo fuerunt duodecim; qui dicitur Didymus : quod interpretatum est dubius, quia de Christi resurrectione præ ceteris fuit incredulus ; non erat cum eis, quando venit Jesus. Huic videtur contrarium quod Lucas habet, duos discipulos regressos a castello Emmaus invenisse congregatos undecim, quorum unus exstitit Thomas. Respondet Augustinus, quod Thomas adfuit redeuntibus illis duobus : quibus loquentibus, Thomas propter aliquam causam exivit, et interim apparuit Christus. Potest etiam dici, quod iste sit sensus verborum Lucæ : Invenerunt congregatos undecim, id est Apostolos, qui pro tunc undecim erant, quamvis non fuerunt omnes collecti. Est quoque consuetudo Scripturæ, ut aliquid attribuatur toti communitati, quia majori vel principaliori ejus competit parti.
paras.en: [[20:24|Now Thomas, one of the twelve|Thomas autem unus ex duodecim]], that is, one of the Apostles, who before Christ's passion were twelve, when Judas was one of them[[Matt 10:3||]]; or, One of the twelve, because when John wrote the present gospel Mathias had succeeded in the place of Judas[[Acts 1:26||]], and so Thomas was one of the Apostles, who with Mathias chosen were twelve; [[20:24|who is called Didymus|qui dicitur Didymus]]: which being interpreted is doubtful, because more than the rest he was unbelieving about Christ's resurrection; [[20:24|was not with them when Jesus came|non erat cum eis, quando venit Jesus]]. Against this seems what Luke has, that the two disciples returning from the village of Emmaus found the eleven gathered together[[Luke 24:33||]], of whom Thomas was one. Augustine answers that Thomas was present when those two returned: while they were speaking, Thomas went out for some reason, and meanwhile Christ appeared. It can also be said that the sense of Luke's words is this: They found the eleven gathered, that is, the Apostles, who were then eleven, though not all were assembled. It is also the custom of Scripture to attribute something to a whole community because it belongs to its greater or chief part.

paras.t: Quæritur, quum Thomas defuerit quando Jesus venit, insufflavit, Spiritum Sanctum largitus est, et dicebat, Quorum remiseritis peccata, etc., an ipse Spiritum Sanctum bis recepit, et potestatem ligandi atque solvendi sortitus est. Dici potest quod post octo dies apparente Jesu, Thomas recuperavit quod in die Paschæ per absentiam suam non accepit. — Insuper, teste Gregorio, divina dispensatione factum est ut Thomas tunc deesset, videlicet ad nostram informationem, quatenus Thoma dubitante propter suam absentiam, Christus appareret frequentius, suamque resurrectionem probaret lucidius.
paras.en: It is asked, since Thomas was absent when Jesus came, breathed, bestowed the Holy Ghost and said, Whose sins you shall forgive, etc., whether he received the Holy Ghost twice and obtained the power of binding and loosing. It can be said that when Jesus appeared after eight days Thomas recovered what he had not received on the day of the Pasch through his absence. — Moreover, as Gregory witnesses, it came about by divine dispensation that Thomas was then absent, namely for our instruction, so that, Thomas doubting because of his absence, Christ might appear more often and prove His resurrection more clearly.

paras.t: Dixerunt ergo ei in domum regresso alii discipuli : Vidimus Dominum. Ille autem dixit eis : Nisi videro in manibus ejus fixuram clavorum, et mittam digitum meum in locum clavorum, hoc est in partes manuum clavis fixas, et mittam manum meam in latus ejus, tangendo lateris aperturam, non credam. Tam durus ad fidem et grossus fuerat Thomas, quod nec tot tantisque testibus credidit ; nec videre satis putavit, sed voluit etiam corpus manu tractare seu tangere. Non enim consideravit omnipotentiam Dei, nec recordabatur verborum Christi quibus prænuntiavit se resurrecturum tertia die, sed quam impossibile esset naturaliter hominem taliter passum resurgere.
paras.en: [[20:25|The other disciples therefore said to him|Dixerunt ergo ei alii discipuli]], when he had come back to the house, [[20:25|We have seen the Lord|Vidimus Dominum]]. [[20:25|But he said to them: Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails and put my finger into the place of the nails|Ille autem dixit eis : Nisi videro in manibus ejus fixuram clavorum, et mittam digitum meum in locum clavorum]], that is, into the parts of the hands pierced by the nails, [[20:25|and put my hand into his side|et mittam manum meam in latus ejus]], touching the opening of the side, [[20:25|I will not believe|non credam]]. So hard and dull towards faith had Thomas been, that he did not believe so many and such witnesses; nor did he think seeing enough, but wished also to handle or touch the body. For he did not consider the omnipotence of God, nor remember the words of Christ by which He foretold that He would rise the third day[[Matt 16:21||]][[Matt 17:22||]][[Matt 20:19||]], but how impossible it would be by nature for a man who had suffered so to rise again.

paras.t: Et post dies octo, hoc est die octava inclusive, iterum erant discipuli ejus intus, id est in domo prædicta, propter metum Judæorum, ut ante, et Thomas cum eis. Puto quod Thomas post præscriptam apparitionem magis quam ante mansit cum Apostolis, timens ne Jesus denuo illis appareret se absente. Venit Jesus januis clausis. Propter quod dixit Manichæus, quod Jesus habuit corpus phantasticum, non attendens omnipotentiam Dei, quæ potest unum corpus per aliud ducere, ambobus integris permanentibus. Et stetit in medio discipulorum, et dixit : Pax vobis. Ista jam semel exposita sunt.
paras.en: [[20:26|And after eight days|Et post dies octo]], that is, on the eighth day counted inclusively, [[20:26|again his disciples were within|iterum erant discipuli ejus intus]], that is, in the said house, for fear of the Jews as before, [[20:26|and Thomas with them|et Thomas cum eis]]. I think that after the appearance described Thomas stayed with the Apostles more than before, fearing lest Jesus should appear to them again in his absence. [[20:26|Jesus cometh, the doors being shut|Venit Jesus januis clausis]]. On account of which the Manichean said that Jesus had a phantom body, not heeding the omnipotence of God, which can pass one body through another, both remaining intact. [[20:26|and stood in the midst|et stetit in medio]] of the disciples, [[20:26|and said: Peace be to you|et dixit: Pax vobis]]. These things have already been explained once.

paras.t: Deinde dicit Thomæ, ostendens se verba illius agnoscere : Infer digitum tuum huc, in locum clavorum manuum mearum, et palpa fixuras earum, et vide manus meas clavis perforatas, et affer manum tuam, et mitte in latus meum, tangendo aperturam illius ; et noli esse incredulus, sed fidelis, quia dixisti te non crediturum, nisi videris ac tetigeris ista. Ecce quanta fecit Christus pro conversione unius, quam pie et caritative se ipsum exhibuit Thomæ discredenti : nam et si Thomas plura aut certiora resurrectionis argumenta petisset, non denegasset ipsi ea Salvator.
paras.en: [[20:27|Then he said to Thomas|Deinde dicit Thomæ]], showing that He knew his words: [[20:27|Put in thy finger hither|Infer digitum tuum huc]], into the place of the nails in My hands, and feel their prints, [[20:27|and see my hands|et vide manus meas]] pierced with the nails, [[20:27|And bring hither the hand and put it into my side|et affer manum tuam, et mitte in latus meum]], touching its opening; [[20:27|And be not faithless, but believing|et noli esse incredulus, sed fidelis]], since thou saidst thou wouldst not believe unless thou didst see and touch these things. See how much Christ did for the conversion of one man, how lovingly and charitably He showed Himself to the unbelieving Thomas: for even had Thomas asked for more or surer proofs of the resurrection, the Saviour would not have denied them to him.

paras.t: Respondit Thomas, et dixit ei : Dominus meus et Deus meus es tu. In quo divinitatem Christi fatetur. Tanta enim evidentia veritatis convictus, corde credidit, et ore confessus est, quod Jesus cujus humanitatem vidit, esset verus Deus, quemadmodum ante passionem ab ipso audivit : Ego et Pater unum sumus. Præterea, an Thomas tetigerit latus et manus Christi, an ex reverentia id omisit, non est certum, nec potest ex textu præsenti determinari : unde diversi de hoc diversimode opinantur.
paras.en: [[20:28|Thomas answered and said to him: My Lord and my God|Respondit Thomas, et dixit ei : Dominus meus et Deus meus]], art Thou. In which he confesses the divinity of Christ. For, convinced by such evidence of the truth, he believed with the heart and confessed with the mouth[[Rom 10:10||]] that Jesus, whose humanity he saw, was true God, as he had heard from Him before the passion: [[John 10:30|I and the Father are one|Ego et Pater unum sumus]]. Further, whether Thomas touched Christ's side and hands, or out of reverence refrained, is not certain, nor can it be determined from the present text: so various men hold various opinions about it.

paras.t: Dixit ei Jesus : Quia vidisti me, Thoma, oculis carnis, quantum ad naturam meam assumptam, credidisti quod non vidisti, videlicet quod sim Deus. Aliud itaque vidit, et aliud credidit. Vidit hominem, et credidit Deum. Beati qui non viderunt, et crediderunt. Hoc aliqui asserunt dictum de aliis discipulis. Sed non apparet : nam discipuli qui aderant, omnes jam viderant Christum. Propterea Augustinus dicit hoc dictum de nobis ac ceteris qui crediderunt, credunt et credent in Christum fide formata, quem non viderunt oculo corporali, quemadmodum Petrus habet : In quem nunc non videntes creditis. Actus enim fidei meritorius est, eo quod ex naturali ratione non habet certitudinem, sed divinæ auctoritati innititur, cui intellectus se subjecit. Qui autem Jesum oculo corporali non viderunt, et tamen credunt, magis innituntur auctoritati divinæ atque Scripturis, quam qui oculo carnis eum intuiti sunt. Ideo sunt nunc beatiores in spe, ceteris paribus : quod addo, quia non est arbitrandum quod aliquis præter Apostolos, qui Christum non vidit, et credidit, sit simpliciter beatior Thoma, quamvis quantum ad aliquid ei præferatur.
paras.en: [[20:29|Jesus saith to him: Because thou hast seen me, Thomas|Dixit ei Jesus : Quia vidisti me, Thoma]], with the eyes of the flesh, as to My assumed nature, [[20:29|thou hast believed|credidisti]] what thou hast not seen, namely that I am God. So he saw one thing and believed another. He saw a man and believed God. [[20:29|blessed are they that have not seen and have believed|Beati qui non viderunt, et crediderunt]]. Some assert this was said of the other disciples. But it does not appear so: for the disciples who were present had all already seen Christ. Therefore Augustine says this was said of us and the others who have believed, believe and will believe in Christ with formed faith [[that is, faith informed by charity]], whom they have not seen with bodily eye, as Peter has it: [[1 Pet 1:8|in whom also now though you see him not, you believe|In quem nunc non videntes creditis]]. For the act of faith is meritorious because it has no certitude from natural reason, but rests on divine authority, to which the intellect has subjected itself. Those who have not seen Jesus with bodily eye and yet believe rest more on divine authority and the Scriptures than those who beheld Him with the eye of flesh. Therefore they are now more blessed in hope, other things being equal: which I add because it is not to be thought that anyone apart from the Apostles who did not see Christ and believed is simply more blessed than Thomas, though in some respect he may be preferred to him.

paras.t: Multa quidem et alia signa fecit Jesus in conspectu discipulorum suorum, quæ non sunt scripta in libro hoc. Hoc intelligi potest, tam de signis quibus Christus se resurrexisse probavit, quorum multa omisit Joannes, et aliqua illorum alii Evangelistæ scripserunt, quam de ceteris miraculis quæ operatus est ante passionem coram discipulis, quorum pauca scribit Joannes ; alii autem Evangelistæ multa illorum describunt signorum. Singuli tamen et omnes aliqua omiserunt, tam de doctrina quam de miraculis Salvatoris. In quo patet insufficientia Scripturæ Evangelistarum per comparationem ad eminentiam operum documentorumque Christi, quæ a nullo mortalium plene possunt describi, secundum doctores.
paras.en: [[20:30|Many other signs also did Jesus in the sight of his disciples, which are not written in this book.|Multa quidem et alia signa fecit Jesus in conspectu discipulorum suorum, quæ non sunt scripta in libro hoc.]] This can be understood both of the signs by which Christ proved that He had risen, many of which John omitted and some of which the other Evangelists wrote, and of the other miracles which He worked before the passion in the presence of the disciples, of which John writes few, while the other Evangelists describe many of those signs. Yet each and all omitted some things, both of the Saviour's teaching and of His miracles. In which the insufficiency of the Evangelists' writing appears in comparison with the eminence of the works and teachings of Christ, which can be fully described by no mortal, according to the doctors.

paras.t: Hæc autem scripta sunt, ut credatis fide per dilectionem operante, quia Jesus est Christus Filius Dei naturalis ac unicus. Per supernaturalia enim opera sua ostendit Jesus se esse Filium Dei : ideo talia scripta sunt, ut qui ea non vidimus, audiendo seu legendo credamus quod Jesus sit Filius Dei. Potius quoque ait Evangelista, Ut credatis quia Jesus est Filius Dei, quam, Filius Virginis, quoniam principalis sua intentio in descriptione hujus evangelii, fuit ostendere Christi divinitatem atque divinam generationem, quia de Christi humanitate et generatione ejus materna, alii Evangelistæ satis scripserunt. Et ut credentes, vitam habeatis gratiæ in præsenti, et vitam gloriæ in futuro. Cognitio enim fidei ordinatur finaliter ad vitam æternam, quæ est visio Dei per speciem. Unde Petrus : Videntes, inquit, exsultabitis lætitia inenarrabili et glorificata, reportantes finem fidei vestræ salutem, fructum animarum vestrarum. Itaque, Vitam habeatis in nomine ejus, id est virtute et gratia Christi, vel in ipso Christo, tanquam in causa et objecto beatitudinis nostræ, quia non est aliud nomen datum hominibus sub cœlo, in quo oporteat nos salvos fieri.
paras.en: [[20:31|But these are written, that you may believe|Hæc autem scripta sunt, ut credatis]] with faith that worketh by charity[[Gal 5:6||]], [[20:31|that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God|quia Jesus est Christus Filius Dei]], natural and only-begotten. For by His supernatural works Jesus showed Himself to be the Son of God: therefore such things were written, so that we who did not see them may, by hearing or reading, believe that Jesus is the Son of God. The Evangelist says, That you may believe that Jesus is the Son of God, rather than, the Son of the Virgin, because his chief intention in writing this gospel was to show Christ's divinity and divine generation, since the other Evangelists wrote enough of Christ's humanity and His generation from His mother. [[20:31|and that believing, you may have life|et ut credentes, vitam habeatis]], the life of grace in the present and the life of glory in the future. For the knowledge of faith is ordered finally to eternal life, which is the vision of God face to face. Whence Peter: [[1 Pet 1:8|believing, shall rejoice with joy unspeakable and glorified|exsultabitis lætitia inenarrabili et glorificata]], he says, seeing, [[1 Pet 1:9|Receiving the end of your faith, even the salvation of your souls|reportantes finem fidei vestræ salutem, fructum animarum vestrarum]]. So, You may have life [[20:31|in his name|in nomine ejus]], that is, by the power and grace of Christ, or in Christ Himself, as in the cause and object of our beatitude, because [[Acts 4:12|there is no other name under heaven given to men, whereby we must be saved|non est aliud nomen datum hominibus sub cœlo, in quo oporteat nos salvos fieri]].

21.title: EXPLANATIO SEQUENTIS PARTIS HUJUS VICESIMI PRIMI CAPITULI : QUUM ERGO PRANDISSENT.
21.title_en: Explanation of the following part of this twenty-first chapter: When therefore they had dined.

paras.t: Facto itaque prandio Christi cum septem discipulis, Dicit Simoni Petro Jesus : Simon Joannis (sic dicitur Petrus, quoniam pater ejus vocabatur Joannes), diligis me plus his? Quum Salomone testante, nemo sciat an amore vel odio dignus sit, cur Christus interrogat Petrum an se diligat, quod esse non potuit sine gratia gratum faciente, quæ facit dignum amore? Rursus, quum teste Apostolo, nemo sciat quid agatur in homine, nisi spiritus ejus, cur Christus sciscitatus est Petrum an diligeret eum plus his, id est ardentius quam alii discipuli qui aderant, quasi Petrus scire posset quantum alii afficerentur ad Christum? — Et respondendum, quod Christus interrogat, non quasi ignorans aut discens, sed docere intendens. Quærit ergo an Petrus diligat eum plus quam alii discipuli, non quod Petrus certitudinaliter scire potuit sine revelatione divina, quod amaret Christum per caritatem infusam, quæ est virtus theologica, vel quod amaret eum plus quam alii : sed ut doceret, quod aliorum prælatus debet non solum diligere Christum, sed etiam debet eum diligere magis ferventer quam alii; imo in omni perfectione et gratia debet abundare atque excellere, ut de plenitudine ejus accipiant universi subditi sui, possitque ad instar angelici hierarchæ gregem sibi commissum et unumquemque subditorum suorum, secundum suam capacitatem, proportionem et indigentiam, purgare, illuminare, perficere. Unde, quamvis secundum jura sufficiat eligere sufficienter bonum sive idoneum, nec oporteat eligere meliorem vel sufficientiorem in foro contentioso, secundum Thomam (aliter electio posset pene semper cassari et irrita fieri, propter quod in foro contentioso judicioque humano sufficit eligere personam idoneam); tamen in foro conscientiæ tenetur eligens meliorem eligere, eum videlicet qui omnibus pensandis pensatis, melior æstimatur pro honore Dei et utilitate Ecclesiæ.
paras.en: The meal of Christ with the seven disciples being over, then, [[21:15|Jesus saith to Simon Peter: Simon, son of John|Dicit Simoni Petro Jesus : Simon Joannis]] (Peter is so called because his father was named John), [[21:15|lovest thou me more than these|diligis me plus his]]? Since, as Solomon witnesses, no man knows whether he be worthy of love or hatred[[Eccles 9:1||]], why does Christ ask Peter whether he loves Him, which could not be without sanctifying grace [gratia gratum faciens, the grace that makes the soul pleasing to God], which makes one worthy of love? Again, since, as the Apostle witnesses, no one knows what goes on in a man save his own spirit[[1 Cor 2:11||]], why did Christ ask Peter whether he loved Him more than these, that is, more ardently than the other disciples present, as if Peter could know how much the others were moved towards Christ? — The answer is that Christ asks, not as one ignorant or learning, but meaning to teach. He asks, then, whether Peter loves Him more than the other disciples, not because Peter could know with certainty without divine revelation that he loved Christ with infused charity, which is a theological virtue, or that he loved Him more than the others; but to teach that the prelate of others ought not only to love Christ, but to love Him more fervently than the others; nay, he ought to abound and excel in all perfection and grace, so that of his fulness all his subjects may receive[[John 1:16||]], and so that, after the likeness of an angelic hierarch, he may purge, illuminate and perfect the flock committed to him and each of his subjects, according to his capacity, proportion and need. Hence, although by law it suffices to elect one sufficiently good or suitable, and it is not necessary to elect the better or more sufficient in the contentious forum [that is, the external court of law], according to Thomas (otherwise an election could almost always be quashed and made void, for which reason in the contentious forum and human judgment it suffices to elect a suitable person); yet in the forum of conscience the elector is bound to elect the better, namely him who, all things to be weighed having been weighed, is judged better for the honour of God and the good of the Church.

paras.t: Dicit ei Petrus : Etiam, Domine, tu scis quia amo te. Paulo ante dixerat Petrus incaute, se præferens aliis : Etsi omnes scandalizati fuerint, ego nunquam scandalizabor. Nunc autem propriam fragilitatem expertus, ampliorique discretione et gratia decoratus, non audet respondere quod plus amet Jesum quam condiscipuli; sed hoc quod sibi constabat asseruit, dicens : Tu scis quia amo te. Quasi dicat : Tu melius scis interiora mea, quam ego ipse, idcirco tuo judicio sto; quod autem ignoro, non dico neque determino. Per quod docemur non præferre nos aliis, nec de illorum interioribus temere judicare, sed in dubiis suspensum dare responsum. Dulcis certe et moderata S. Petri responsio.
paras.en: [[21:15|He saith to him|Dicit ei]] Peter: [[21:15|Yea, Lord, thou knowest that I love thee|Etiam, Domine, tu scis quia amo te]]. A little before, Peter had said rashly, preferring himself to the others: [[Matt 26:33|Although all shall be scandalized|Etsi omnes scandalizati fuerint, ego nunquam scandalizabor]]. But now, having experienced his own frailty, and adorned with greater discretion and grace, he dares not answer that he loves Jesus more than his fellow disciples; but he affirmed what was clear to him, saying: Thou knowest that I love thee. As if to say: Thou knowest my inward parts better than I myself, therefore I stand by Thy judgment; what I do not know I neither say nor determine. By this we are taught not to prefer ourselves to others, nor rashly to judge their inward parts, but in doubtful matters to give a suspended answer. Sweet indeed and measured is the answer of St Peter.

paras.t: Dicit ei Jesus : Pasce agnos meos. Tanquam dicat Salvator : In hoc apparebit quod diligas me, si digne paveris servulos meos, homines pios et innocentes. Vel sic : Pasce agnos meos. Quia me diligis, aptus es pascere gregem populi mei, nec aliquid majus requiro mihi dari a te ex dilectione tua ad me, nisi ut spiritualiter foveas plebem credentem. Zelus enim animarum, est sacrificium Deo gratissimum. Debet autem prælatus pascere subditos suos verbo instructionis, exemplo sanctæ conversationis, temporali quoque subsidio dum ratio exigit. Porro de hac materia, scilicet quo modo prælatus pascere debeat gregem Christi sanguine liberatum, dicta sunt multa capitulo decimo. Possumus autem per agnos intelligere non solum innocentes, pios et puros, sed quoscumque quos Deus prædestinavit ad gratiam talem, qui finaliter agni erunt, et pascua vitæ possidebunt æternæ.
paras.en: [[21:15|He saith to him|Dicit ei]] Jesus: [[21:15|Feed my lambs|Pasce agnos meos]]. As if the Saviour said: In this it will appear that thou lovest Me, if thou worthily feed My little servants, men devout and innocent. Or thus: Feed my lambs. Because thou lovest Me, thou art fit to feed the flock of My people, and I require nothing greater to be given Me by thee out of thy love for Me than that thou cherish spiritually the believing people. For zeal for souls is a sacrifice most pleasing to God. The prelate ought to feed his subjects with the word of instruction, the example of holy living, and also temporal help when reason requires it. Much was said on this matter, namely how a prelate ought to feed the flock of Christ freed by His blood, on the tenth chapter [the margin refers to Arts. XXV and XXVI]. By lambs we may understand not only the innocent, devout and pure, but all whom God has predestined to such grace, who will at the last be lambs and will possess the pastures of eternal life.

paras.t: Dicit ei iterum : Simon Joannis, diligis me? Quæritur, an Petrus certitudinaliter scivit se diligere Christum. Dicendum, quod Apostoli plus post receptionem illam plenariam Spiritus Sancti factam in die Pentecostes, sciverunt se primitias Spiritus esse sortitos, atque in bono confirmatos : ideo certitudinaliter sciebant se Christum amare. Ideo Paulus certissime loquitur : Quis nos separabit a caritate Dei? An vero post receptionem Spiritus Sancti per insufflationem Christi, quæ hanc interrogationem præcessit, Apostoli certitudinaliter sciverint se esse in caritate et gratia indesinenter, quousque Spiritum Sanctum plenius acceperunt, non est adeo certum. Si autem Petrus hac vice scivit certitudinaliter se Christum diligere dilectione meritoria et infusa, hoc fuit per revelationem. Verumtamen, palam est quod Petrus certissime novit, et vehementer experiebatur seu sensit, quod amavit Christum, saltem amore naturali et acquisito. Sensit enim se æstuare in Christi affectu atque memoria, præsertim in ejus adspectu. Ait illi : Etiam, Domine, tu scis quia amo te. Dicit ei Jesus : Pasce agnos meos. Ista jam semel dicta sunt atque exposita.
paras.en: [[21:16|He saith to him again: Simon, son of John, lovest thou me?|Dicit ei iterum : Simon Joannis, diligis me]]? It is asked whether Peter knew with certainty that he loved Christ. It must be said that the Apostles, rather after that full reception of the Holy Ghost made on the day of Pentecost, knew that they had received the firstfruits of the Spirit[[Rom 8:23||]] and were confirmed in good: therefore they knew with certainty that they loved Christ. Hence Paul speaks most surely: [[Rom 8:35|Who then shall separate us from the love of Christ?|Quis nos separabit a caritate Dei]]? But whether after receiving the Holy Ghost through Christ's breathing upon them[[John 20:22||]], which preceded this questioning, the Apostles knew with certainty that they were unceasingly in charity and grace until they received the Holy Ghost more fully, is not so certain. If Peter on this occasion knew with certainty that he loved Christ with a meritorious and infused love, this was by revelation. Nevertheless it is plain that Peter knew most surely, and vehemently experienced or felt, that he loved Christ, at least with a natural and acquired love. For he felt himself burn with affection for Christ and with the memory of Him, especially in His sight. [[21:16|He saith to him: yea, Lord, thou knowest that I love thee|Ait illi : Etiam, Domine, tu scis quia amo te]]. [[21:16|He saith to him: Feed my lambs|Dicit ei Jesus : Pasce agnos meos]]. These have already been said once and expounded.

paras.t: Dicit ei tertio : Simon Joannis, amas me? Ter Christus interrogat et examinat Petrum de sua dilectione, quia prælatus diligere debet Deum cordiali affectu, affectuosis sermonibus, caritativis operibus; et iterum, ut Petrus trina divini amoris confessione, recompensam faciat pro trina Christi timorosa negatione; vel ad insinuandum quod promovendi ad prælationem, sæpe ac diligenter discutiendi seu considerandi sunt, an sint vere idonei, itemque in caritate præcipui. Contristatus est Petrus, quia dixit ei tertio, Amas me? Videbatur enim quasi Christus responsionem suam non approbaret, nec crederet verbis ipsius. Et forte timuit quod ideo Christus toties verba sua replicavit, quia vellet ei aliquid prænuntiare, in quo ostenderetur non diligere Christum : sicut quum fiducialiter dixit, Animam meam pro te ponam, audivit : Non cantabit gallus, donec ter me neges. Et dicit ei : Domine, tu omnia cordis arcana, et quidquid fuit, est vel erit, nosti, non solum per naturam divinam, sed insuper secundum naturam assumptam, per scientiam concreatam seu inditam; tu scis quia amo te, ideo non oportet te amplius interrogare, et me famulum tuum affligere.
paras.en: [[21:17|He said to him the third time: Simon, son of John, lovest thou me?|Dicit ei tertio : Simon Joannis, amas me]]? Three times Christ questions and examines Peter about his love, because a prelate ought to love God with heartfelt affection, affectionate words and charitable works; and again, so that Peter by a threefold confession of divine love might make amends for his threefold fearful denial of Christ[[Matt 26:69||]]; or to intimate that those to be promoted to prelacy must be often and carefully examined and considered, whether they be truly suitable and also eminent in charity. [[21:17|Peter was grieved because he had said to him the third time: Lovest thou me?|Contristatus est Petrus, quia dixit ei tertio, Amas me]]? For it seemed as though Christ did not approve his answer nor believe his words. And perhaps he feared that Christ repeated His words so often because He wished to foretell him something in which it would be shown that he did not love Christ: as when he said confidently, [[John 13:37|I will lay down my life for thee|Animam meam pro te ponam]], he heard: [[John 13:38|the cock shall not crow, till thou deny me thrice|Non cantabit gallus, donec ter me neges]]. [[21:17|And he said to him: Lord, thou knowest all things|et dixit ei: Domine, tu omnia nosti]]: all the secrets of the heart, and whatever was, is or shall be, not only by the divine nature, but moreover according to the assumed nature, by concreated or infused knowledge; [[21:17|thou knowest that I love thee|tu scis quia amo te]], therefore Thou needest not question further and afflict me Thy servant.

paras.t: Dicit ei : Pasce oves meas. Superius dixit bis, Pasce agnos meos; nunc ait, Pasce oves meas. Unde per agnos intelligendi sunt incipientes et proficientes, qui solidum cibum capere nequeunt. Quibus loquitur Paulus ad Corinthios : Tanquam parvulis in Christo, lac vobis potum dedi, non escam. Jam autem per oves designantur perfecti, qui pro consuetudine exercitatos habent sensus, et quasi aliorum exstant parentes. Præterea Christus committit Petro ter gregem suum, ad insinuandum quod prælatus pascere debet sibi commissos prece mentali, instructione vocali, operationeque vitali, triplici cibo, ut dictum est; vel ideo, ut prælati agnoscant quantam habeat Christus diligentiam, dilectionem et curam pro suis fidelibus, quam sollicite velit eos custodiri, quam districte requiret a pastoribus rationem de eis. Et quia prælati debent esse parati ad moriendum pro fide, pro justitia, pro Christo, pro grege commisso, ideo consequenter Christus prædicit Petro de qualitate sui martyrii.
paras.en: [[21:17|He said to him: Feed my sheep|Dicit ei : Pasce oves meas]]. Above He twice said, Feed my lambs; now He says, Feed my sheep. Hence by lambs are understood beginners and those making progress, who cannot take solid food. To such Paul speaks to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 3:1|as unto little ones in Christ|Tanquam parvulis in Christo]], [[1 Cor 3:2|I gave you milk to drink, not meat|lac vobis potum dedi, non escam]]. But by sheep are signified the perfect, who by custom have their senses exercised[[Heb 5:14||]], and are as it were parents of others. Moreover Christ commits His flock to Peter three times to intimate that a prelate ought to feed those committed to him with mental prayer, spoken instruction and the working of his life, a threefold food, as has been said; or so that prelates may recognise how great diligence, love and care Christ has for His faithful, how anxiously He wills them to be guarded, how strictly He will require an account of them from the pastors. And because prelates ought to be ready to die for the faith, for justice, for Christ, for the flock committed to them, Christ accordingly foretells to Peter the manner of his martyrdom.

paras.t: Amen, amen dico tibi, quum esses junior annis quam nunc, quando etiam moribus junior eras quam modo, cingebas te cingulo materiali ad lumbos, cingebas te quoque cingulo continentiæ quantum ad appetitum concupiscibilem, et ab illicitis te restringebas. Unde in Actibus Apostolorum Petrus testatur : Nunquam comedi commune quid aut immundum. Et ambulabas ubi volebas, pergendo de loco ad locum ad libitum tuum, tanquam non ligatus ab aliquo, itemque prædicta faciendo propria libertate, sine violentia et compulsione. Quum autem senueris ætate et gratia, scilicet morte tua instante, quando dicturus es, Velox est depositio tabernaculi mei; extendes manus tuas ad brachia crucis cui appenderis : quod utique Petrus promptissime fecit secundum rationem et appetitum superiorem; et alius te cinget, hoc est, apparitor imperatoris Neronis manus tuas cruci alligabit. Non enim clavis affixus, sed funibus alligatus fuit patibulo crucis. Ligavit etiam Petrum in urbe Roma antequam educeretur ad mortem. Et ducet te quo tu non vis, hoc est ad locum passionis, et ad amaritudinem mortis, quam secundum naturalem ac sensitivum appetitum abhorrebis atque refugies, quamvis secundum appetitum intellectivum eam libentissime patieris, cupiens dissolvi et esse mecum in regno. Verumtamen appetitus iste inferior refugiens mortem, fuit in Petro finaliter subditus rationis judicio atque imperio, ita quod non timuit immoderate eos qui corpus occiderunt.
paras.en: [[21:18|Amen, amen, I say to thee, When thou wast younger|Amen, amen dico tibi, quum esses junior]] in years than now, when thou wast also younger in character than at present, [[21:18|thou didst gird thyself|cingebas te]] with a material girdle about the loins; thou didst gird thyself also with the girdle of continence as to the concupiscible appetite, and didst restrain thyself from things unlawful. Hence in the Acts of the Apostles Peter testifies: [[Acts 10:14|I never did eat any thing that is common and unclean|Nunquam comedi commune quid aut immundum]]. [[21:18|and didst walk where thou wouldst|Et ambulabas ubi volebas]], going from place to place at thy pleasure, as one bound by no one, and also doing the aforesaid by thine own freedom, without violence and compulsion. [[21:18|But when thou shalt be old|Quum autem senueris]] in age and grace, namely when thy death is at hand, when thou shalt say, [[2 Pet 1:14|the laying away of this my tabernacle is at hand|Velox est depositio tabernaculi mei]], [[21:18|thou shalt stretch forth thy hands|extendes manus tuas]] to the arms of the cross on which thou shalt hang: which Peter indeed did most readily according to reason and the higher appetite; [[21:18|and another shall gird thee|et alius te cinget]], that is, the officer of the emperor Nero shall bind thy hands to the cross. For he was not fixed with nails but bound with ropes to the gibbet of the cross. He also bound Peter in the city of Rome before he was led out to death. [[21:18|and lead thee whither thou wouldst not|Et ducet te quo tu non vis]], that is, to the place of passion and the bitterness of death, which according to the natural and sensitive appetite thou wilt abhor and shrink from, although according to the intellective appetite thou wilt suffer it most willingly, [[Phil 1:23|desire to be dissolved and to be with Christ|cupiens dissolvi et esse mecum]] in the kingdom. Yet that lower appetite shrinking from death was in Peter finally subject to the judgment and command of reason, so that he did not immoderately fear those who killed the body[[Matt 10:28||]] [the margin reads Matth. x, 28].

paras.t: Sancti etenim et perfecti viri appetunt et non appetunt mortem sive martyrium, quemadmodum æger vult et non vult potum amarum. Æger namque secundum sensitivum appetitum refugit potionem amaram, præsertim si consideretur potio amara secundum se, in quantum est afflictiva. Porro secundum rationem et voluntatem intellectivam vult eam, maxime prout est valetudinis inductiva. Sic virtuosi appetunt mortem sive martyrium secundum rationem, in quantum est janua quædam ad vitam beatam; secundum appetitum vero sensitivum refugiunt eam, prout est ultimum maximumque terribilium, secundum Philosophum. Unde hoc modo et Christus refugiens mortem : Pater, inquit, transeat a me calix iste. Sed in Christo, ratio prævenit et imperavit hunc mortis timorem. In ceteris autem, motus hujusmodi præveniunt rationem, quia et primi motus non sunt in potestate nostra. Propter quod Paulus decollandus fecit sibi oculos circumligari, ne ensem cernens venientem, pateretur subitum motum naturalis timoris.
paras.en: For holy and perfect men both desire and do not desire death or martyrdom, as a sick man wills and does not will a bitter draught. The sick man by his sensitive appetite shrinks from the bitter potion, especially if the bitter potion be considered in itself, as it is painful. But according to reason and the intellective will he wills it, chiefly as it brings about health. So the virtuous desire death or martyrdom according to reason, inasmuch as it is a kind of door to the blessed life; but according to the sensitive appetite they shrink from it, as it is the last and greatest of terrible things, according to the Philosopher [Aristotle]. Hence in this way Christ too, shrinking from death, says: [[Matt 26:39|Father, if it be possible, let this chalice pass from me|Pater, inquit, transeat a me calix iste]]. But in Christ reason went before and commanded this fear of death. In others such movements go before reason, for first movements [that is, the spontaneous stirrings of passion before deliberation] are not in our power. For this reason Paul, when about to be beheaded, had his eyes bandaged, lest seeing the sword coming he should suffer a sudden movement of natural fear.

paras.t: Deinde sequuntur verba Evangelistæ exponentis verba Christi præhabita. Hoc autem, id est præinductum sermonem parabolicum de Petri martyrio, dixit Jesus, significans qua morte clarificaturus esset Deum, id est, per verba illa Christus insinuavit quali martyrio Petrus honoraret Deum, moriendo pro fide et æquitate ipsius. Quemadmodum enim justi clarificant Deum recte conversando, quia in sua conversatione testantur et pandunt quod Deus sit sanctus, sublimis et justus; sic pro justitia moriendo, ipsum clarificant, quia testantur Deum tantæ esse veritatis, æquitatis, dignitatis et amabilitatis, ut potius sit moriendum quam ab illo aliqualiter recedendum. Propter quod ad Philippenses primo Apostolus loquitur : In omni fiducia magnificabitur Christus in corpore meo, sive per vitam, sive per mortem; mihi enim vivere Christus est, et mori lucrum.
paras.en: Then follow the words of the Evangelist expounding the words of Christ just given. [[21:19|And this he said|Hoc autem dixit]], that is, the figurative saying just set down about Peter's martyrdom, Jesus said, [[21:19|signifying by what death he should glorify God|significans qua morte clarificaturus esset Deum]]: that is, by those words Christ intimated by what martyrdom Peter would honour God, dying for His faith and justice. For as the just glorify God by living rightly, because in their conduct they bear witness and make known that God is holy, sublime and just; so by dying for justice they glorify Him, because they bear witness that God is of such truth, justice, dignity and loveliness that one must rather die than in any way depart from Him. Hence the Apostle says in the first chapter to the Philippians: [[Phil 1:20|with all confidence, as always, so now also, shall Christ be magnified in my body, whether it be by life or by death|In omni fiducia magnificabitur Christus in corpore meo, sive per vitam, sive per mortem]]; [[Phil 1:21|For to me, to live is Christ: and to die is gain|mihi enim vivere Christus est, et mori lucrum]].

paras.t: Et quum hoc dixisset, hoc est, postquam Jesus prædixit Petro qua morte clarificaret Deum, dicit ei : Sequere me. Postquam enim Jesus præmemorata disseruit, surrexit de loco convivii, cœpitque abire, et dixit Petro, Sequere me, hortans eum ad corporalem sui imitationem propter mysticam significationem. Jam enim verbis reseravit Petro quod crucifigendus esset. Volens ergo id ipsum facto præsignare, locutus est ei : Sequere me. Tanquam dicat : Per hanc materialem sequelam ad quam te moneo, hoc designo, quod spiritualiter imitaturus es me, sustinendo mortem crucis propter justitiam sicut et ego. Jam nempe sæpe prædixi, quod sicut Prophetæ interdum prophetaverunt verbis, aliquando factis, pariformiter Christus nunc verbis, nunc factis aliqua prænuntiavit. Ideo quoque ait, Sequere me, quatenus Petrus exemplo Christi confortaretur ad sustinendum crucis supplicium.
paras.en: [[21:19|And when he had said this|Et quum hoc dixisset]], that is, after Jesus had foretold to Peter by what death he would glorify God, [[21:19|he saith to him: Follow me|dicit ei : Sequere me]]. For after Jesus had discoursed of the aforesaid things, He rose from the place of the meal and began to go away, and said to Peter, Follow me, exhorting him to a bodily following of Him for the sake of a mystical signification. For He had already disclosed to Peter in words that he was to be crucified. Wishing therefore to foreshow the same by a deed, He said to him: Follow me. As if to say: By this material following to which I urge thee I signify that thou shalt imitate Me spiritually, enduring the death of the cross for justice as I also do. I have indeed often said already that, as the Prophets sometimes prophesied by words and sometimes by deeds, likewise Christ foretold some things now by words, now by deeds. He says, Follow me, also so that Peter might be strengthened by Christ's example to endure the punishment of the cross.

paras.t: Conversus Petrus. Christo enim dicente, Sequere me, orsus est Petrus ambulare corporali gressu post eum. Quod quum faceret, sensit alium quemdam venire post se : propterea, retro adspiciens, vidit quis esset. Sic ergo conversus, vidit illum discipulum quem diligebat Jesus, sequentem motu progressivo : quia ut innuit Augustinus, nec Petrus, neque Joannes cognovit propter quid dixerat Jesus : Sequere me. Qui et recubuit in Cœna super pectus ejus, et dixit : Domine, quis est qui tradet te? Per hanc circumlocutionem significat beatissimus Evangelista se ipsum. Non enim ad sui ipsius jactantiam toties commemorat se specialiter dilectum a Jesu; sed ut tanto beneficio gratus consistat, et quia dulcissimum sibi fuit recolere quam affectuose ac familiariter se habuit Jesus ad eum : inferioribus quippe magnum est a superiori specialiter diligi.
paras.en: [[21:20|Peter turning about|Conversus Petrus]]. For when Christ said, Follow me, Peter began to walk with bodily steps after Him. As he did so, he perceived someone else coming after him; therefore, looking back, he saw who it was. Thus turned, then, he [[21:20|saw that disciple whom Jesus loved following|vidit illum discipulum quem diligebat Jesus, sequentem]] with bodily motion: for, as Augustine intimates, neither Peter nor John knew why Jesus had said, Follow me. [[21:20|who also leaned on his breast at supper and said: Lord, who is he that shall betray thee?|Qui et recubuit in Cœna super pectus ejus, et dixit : Domine, quis est qui tradet te?]]? By this circumlocution the most blessed Evangelist signifies himself[[John 13:23||]][[John 13:25||]]. For it is not to boast of himself that he so often mentions that he was specially loved by Jesus; but to remain grateful for so great a benefit, and because it was most sweet to him to recall how affectionately and familiarly Jesus behaved towards him: for to inferiors it is a great thing to be specially loved by a superior.

paras.t: Hunc ergo quum vidisset Petrus, dicit ad Jesum : Domine, hic autem quid aget vel patietur pro te? quid ei committis? qua morte clarificaturus est Deum? Sollicitus fuit Petrus pro condiscipulo familiari ac prædilecto; nec dubium quin in bonis gratiæ sibi collatis et conferendis, desideravit eum habere consortem, videlicet in cura pastorali atque martyrio.
paras.en: [[21:21|Him therefore when Peter had seen, he saith to Jesus: Lord, and what|Hunc ergo quum vidisset Petrus, dicit ad Jesum : Domine, hic autem quid]] shall he do or suffer for Thee? What dost Thou commit to him? By what death shall he glorify God? Peter was solicitous for his intimate and dearly loved fellow disciple; and no doubt he desired to have him as partner in the goods of grace bestowed and to be bestowed on himself, namely in pastoral care and martyrdom.

paras.t: Dicit ei Jesus : Sic eum volo manere, hoc est, in carne mortali volo Joannem perseverare sine martyrio, utpote in pace, donec veniam ad eum in hora mortis ejus, vocaturus et educturus eum de præsentis peregrinationis exsilio ad æternæ beatitudinis regnum. Quid ad te interrogare de tali secreto futuro?* Quamvis enim, ut in Ecclesiastico legitur, unicuique mandavit Deus de proximo suo, et juxta Pauli doctrinam, debemus singuli quærere, non quæ nostra sunt, sed quæ aliorum; non tamen debemus anxiari, curiose scrutari vel sciscitari quid Deus ordinavit de proximis nostris, quantum ad genus mortis eorum, et quoad occulta futura. Unde Apostolis de tali negotio quærentibus, Christus respondit : Non est vestrum nosse tempora vel momenta quæ Pater posuit in sua potestate.
paras.en: [[22|placeholder]]

paras.t: Quidam præterea hæc verba Christi sic intellexerunt, quod insinuaverit Joannem non moriturum ante diem finalis judicii, quando venturus est Christus in majestate et gloria. Unde quidam dixerunt eum translatum in paradisum terrestrem cum Elia et Enoch, cum quibus aliqui dicunt eum rediturum, et prædicaturum contra Antichristum, atque ab illo occidendum : quatenus sicut unus translatus est in paradisum ante legem, videlicet Enoch, qui fuit ante diluvium, et alter sub lege, puta Elias; sic unus sub gratia translatus credatur, ac per hoc tres, utpote de quolibet tempore unus, venturi sint contra Antichristum. Quibus repugnare videtur, quod in Apocalypsi multa dicuntur de his qui prædicaturi sunt contra Antichristum, qui non asseruntur nisi duo. De quibus in Apocalypsi Dominus loquitur : Dabo duobus testibus meis, et prophetabunt diebus mille ducentis sexaginta; et quum finierint testimonium suum, bestia quæ ascendit de abysso, occidet eos. Alii vero dixerunt Joannem dormientem jacere in monumento ejus apud Ephesum : quia et in loco sepulcri scaturitio quædam percipitur et ebullitio terræ, quod dicunt causari ex ejus anhelitu. Dicunt quoque, quod in fine mundi morietur pro Christo : quia ut ait Psalmista, Quis est homo qui vivet, et non videbit mortem? Itemque Apostolus ad Hebræos : Statutum est hominibus semel mori, post hoc autem judicium. Has opiniones non approbat Augustinus. Non enim videtur quod Christus prædilectum discipulum tam diu retardavit a gloria, maxime quod jaceat in sepulcro ut dormiens. Communiter ergo tenetur quod mortuus sit. Et asserunt quidam, quod in anima et corpore sit glorificatus in cœlo : hoc tamen incertum est.
paras.en: Some, moreover, understood these words of Christ thus: that He intimated that John would not die before the day of the last judgment, when Christ shall come in majesty and glory[[Matt 25:31||]]. Hence some said that he was translated into the earthly paradise with Elias and Enoch, with whom some say he will return and preach against Antichrist and be slain by him: so that, as one was translated into paradise before the law, namely Enoch, who lived before the flood[[Gen 5:24||]], and another under the law, namely Elias[[4 Kings 2:11||]], so one may be believed translated under grace, and thus three, one from each age, will come against Antichrist. Against which it seems to tell that in the Apocalypse many things are said of those who are to preach against Antichrist, and they are stated to be only two. Of them the Lord speaks in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 11:3|And I will give unto my two witnesses: and they shall prophesy, a thousand two hundred sixty days|Dabo duobus testibus meis, et prophetabunt diebus mille ducentis sexaginta]]; [[Apoc 11:7|And when they shall have finished their testimony, the beast that ascendeth out of the abyss shall make war against them and shall|et quum finierint testimonium suum, bestia quæ ascendit de abysso, occidet eos]]. Others said that John lies sleeping in his tomb at Ephesus, because in the place of the sepulchre a certain welling up and bubbling of the earth is perceived, which they say is caused by his breath. They say too that at the end of the world he will die for Christ, because, as the Psalmist says, [[Ps 88:49|Who is the man that shall live, and not see death|Quis est homo qui vivet, et non videbit mortem]]? And the Apostle to the Hebrews: [[Heb 9:27|it is appointed unto men once to die, and after this the judgment|Statutum est hominibus semel mori, post hoc autem judicium]]. Augustine does not approve these opinions. For it does not seem that Christ would have kept His beloved disciple so long from glory, especially that he should lie in the tomb as one sleeping. It is commonly held, therefore, that he is dead. And some assert that he is glorified in heaven in soul and body: this, however, is uncertain.

paras.t: Exivit ergo sermo iste inter fratres, quod discipulus ille non moritur. Ista sunt verba Evangelistæ narrantis qualiter discipuli tunc præsentes intellexerunt verba Christi. Putabant enim quod Jesus significaret Joannem non esse moriturum : et quia erraverunt in hoc, idcirco excludit Joannes hunc sensum. Et non dixit Jesus, quia non moritur, id est, per verba sua non significavit quod Joannes moriturus non esset. Sed dixit : Sic eum volo manere donec veniam (secundum sensum prætactum), quid ad te? Hæc enim fuerunt verba Christi, quæ modo exposita sunt. Legitur autem in vita B. Joannis evangelistæ, quod imminente obitu ejus, venit ad eum Dominus Jesus cum Apostolis, invitans eum ad felicissimam epulationem electorum in patria. Ideo Christus dixit : Sic eum volo manere donec veniam.
